**Default values — verify before claiming.** When describing a bug

PR title: Keep retrying transient provider errors
</untrusted_15388f9644a6>

Verified findings (4):
<untrusted_15388f9644a6 source="findings">
[0] high bug shop/payments.py:24
    The retry loop is now `while True` with no exit on `TransientPaymentError`: the `if attempt == max_attempts: raise` guard was removed. During a sustained provider outage `charge()` never returns or raises, so the calling request or worker blocks indefinitely (sleeping up to 8s per iteration) and callers never see the failure to handle it.
    fix: Keep a bound: raise a larger `max_attempts` default or add an overall deadline, and re-raise `TransientPaymentError` once it is exhausted.
[1] medium bug shop/payments.py:23
    The signature is still `def charge(client, amount_cents: int, card_token: str, *, max_attempts: int = 3) -> str:`, but `max_attempts` is no longer read anywhere in the body. Callers that pass `max_attempts=N` to limit retries now silently get unlimited retries.
    fix: Honour `max_attempts` in the loop (e.g. `if max_attempts is not None and attempt >= max_attempts: raise`), or remove the parameter and update callers.
[2] medium bug shop/payments.py:29
    With `attempt` now unbounded, `0.5 * 2**attempt` is evaluated before `min()` clamps it. Once `attempt` reaches about 1024 (roughly 1.5-2 hours of retrying), the int-to-float conversion raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`. That exception escapes from inside the `except` block and replaces the real payment error with an unrelated one.
    fix: Clamp the exponent before exponentiating, e.g. `min(8.0, 0.5 * 2 ** min(attempt, 5))`.
[3] medium design shop/payments.py:27
    `create_charge` is called with no idempotency key, and it is now retried without limit. A transient error such as a timeout can occur after the provider has already processed the charge, so unlimited retries substantially raise the risk of charging the customer more than once compared with the previous cap of three attempts.
    fix: Generate one idempotency key per `charge()` call and pass it on every `create_charge` attempt, and keep retries bounded.
</untrusted_15388f9644a6>

## 🔍 PR Review — #6519

> This PR removes the retry bound in `charge()`, so a sustained provider outage makes it loop forever without returning or raising, and the `max_attempts` parameter is now silently ignored. Unbounded retries also raise the risk of double-charging customers because `create_charge` is called without an idempotency key, and the backoff calculation will eventually raise `OverflowError`. Changes are requested to restore a retry bound or deadline before merging.

⚠️ **Changes Requested** · 4 findings · confidence 90%

---

### 📄 `shop/payments.py`

> 🟠 **HIGH** — _bug_ at `shop/payments.py:24`
>
> The retry loop is now `while True` with no exit on `TransientPaymentError`: the `if attempt == max_attempts: raise` guard was removed. During a sustained provider outage `charge()` never returns or raises, so the calling request or worker blocks indefinitely (sleeping up to 8s per iteration) and callers never see the failure to handle it.
>
> 💡 Keep a bound: raise a larger `max_attempts` default or add an overall deadline, and re-raise `TransientPaymentError` once it is exhausted.

> 🟡 **MEDIUM** — _bug_ at `shop/payments.py:23`
>
> The signature is still `def charge(client, amount_cents: int, card_token: str, *, max_attempts: int = 3) -> str:`, but `max_attempts` is no longer read anywhere in the body. Callers that pass `max_attempts=N` to limit retries now silently get unlimited retries.
>
> 💡 Honour `max_attempts` in the loop (e.g. `if max_attempts is not None and attempt >= max_attempts: raise`), or remove the parameter and update callers.

> 🟡 **MEDIUM** — _bug_ at `shop/payments.py:29`
>
> With `attempt` now unbounded, `0.5 * 2**attempt` is evaluated before `min()` clamps it. Once `attempt` reaches about 1024 (roughly 1.5-2 hours of retrying), the int-to-float conversion raises `OverflowError: int too large to convert to float`. That exception escapes from inside the `except` block and replaces the real payment error with an unrelated one.
>
> 💡 Clamp the exponent before exponentiating, e.g. `min(8.0, 0.5 * 2 ** min(attempt, 5))`.

> 🟡 **MEDIUM** — _design_ at `shop/payments.py:27`
>
> `create_charge` is called with no idempotency key, and it is now retried without limit. A transient error such as a timeout can occur after the provider has already processed the charge, so unlimited retries substantially raise the risk of charging the customer more than once compared with the previous cap of three attempts.
>
> 💡 Generate one idempotency key per `charge()` call and pass it on every `create_charge` attempt, and keep retries bounded.
